security_audit.summary: AI adjudication found the static findings to be false positives caused by documentation syntax, ASO terminology, and installation examples. No prompt injection, malicious command execution, unauthorized filesystem access, or network behavior was found in the reviewed evidence.

remediation.issue: Markdown backticks are repeatedly flagged as command execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep code fences clearly labeled as examples and avoid shell-like snippets unless they are necessary for installation.

remediation.issue: Installation instructions reference hidden .claude skill directories.
remediation.suggestion: State that users must run installation commands manually and that the skill does not modify these paths by itself.

remediation.issue: Review and launch guidance mentions device, platform, and market research terms that can trigger scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Phrase these references as app-store testing or support context to reduce ambiguity for automated review.

content.value_statement: Mobile teams need better organic discovery and clearer store listings. This skill turns app details, review data, and launch goals into practical ASO recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Analyzes target keywords for search potential, competition, relevance, and long-tail opportunities.
Generates platform-specific metadata for Apple App Store and Google Play Store limits.
Compares competitor metadata, keywords, ratings, visual assets, and positioning gaps.
Calculates ASO health scores across metadata, ratings, keywords, and conversion metrics.
Plans A/B tests for titles, icons, screenshots, and other store listing changes.
Builds pre-launch and update checklists for Apple and Google store submissions.
limitations: Keyword volume and competitor metrics are estimates, not official Apple or Google data.
Review analysis depends on review data supplied by the user or available public exports.
Store policies and algorithm behavior can change, so final guidance should be verified.
The skill focuses on organic ASO and does not plan paid acquisition campaigns.

use_cases.title: Launch a New Mobile App
use_cases.description: Create keywords, metadata, launch timing, and submission checklists before the first public release.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Listing
use_cases.description: Audit current metadata, compare competitors, and prioritize changes that can improve organic discovery.

use_cases.title: Turn Reviews Into Product Work
use_cases.description: Analyze review sentiment, identify common complaints, and draft response themes for store reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Start Keyword Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner ASO research for a new app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to research ASO keywords for my app. My app name is [name], category is [category], audience is [audience], and core features are [features].

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Store Metadata
prompt_templates.scenario: Rewrite Apple and Google store listing text.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to optimize my store metadata for Apple App Store and Google Play. Current title: [title]. Current description: [description]. Target keywords: [keywords].

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Competitors
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare competing listings and find gaps.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare these competitors: [competitors]. Focus on metadata, keyword strategy, ratings, screenshots, and opportunities for my app: [app details].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Launch Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a full ASO launch plan for [launch date]. Include metadata checks, visual asset checks, review readiness, test priorities, and timing recommendations.

output_examples.input: A productivity app wants keyword ideas for task planning and team collaboration.
output_examples.output: A ranked keyword shortlist with relevance scores, competition notes, long-tail opportunities, and recommended placement in title, subtitle, or description.

output_examples.input: An app team provides current Apple and Google listing copy plus target keywords.
output_examples.output: Rewritten title options, short description guidance, full description structure, Apple keyword field suggestions, and character-limit validation.

output_examples.input: A product manager shares recent app reviews and asks what to fix first.
output_examples.output: Sentiment summary, recurring complaint themes, top feature requests, issue priorities, and professional review response templates.

best_practices: Provide current metadata, target audience, category, competitors, and real performance metrics when available.
Validate all final recommendations against current Apple and Google policy pages before release.
Test one major listing change at a time so results can be attributed clearly.
anti_patterns: Do not target keywords that are unrelated to the actual app experience.
Do not copy competitor metadata without checking brand, policy, and relevance risks.
Do not treat estimated keyword volume or ASO score outputs as guaranteed store performance.

faq.question: Does this skill submit apps to the stores?
faq.answer: No. It prepares recommendations and checklists, but users submit apps through App Store Connect and Google Play Console.

faq.question: Can it optimize both Apple and Google listings?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes platform-specific character limits and metadata fields for Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

faq.question: Does it use paid advertising data?
faq.answer: No. The scope is organic discovery, listing conversion, reviews, localization, testing, and launch planning.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide app category, features, target audience, current metadata, competitors, keywords, ratings, reviews, and conversion metrics if available.

faq.question: Can it analyze private app reviews automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can analyze review data that you provide, but it does not access private store dashboards.

faq.question: Is the guidance always current with store policies?
faq.answer: No. Store policies change, so verify important launch and compliance recommendations with official store documentation.
